You hold Bitcoin and Ethereum. Selling either triggers capital gains tax and ends your exposure to future appreciation. Borrowing against them lets you access cash while keeping your position intact. The market now offers many platforms that accept BTC and ETH as collateral—but they work very differently. Some offer revolving credit lines with no repayment deadlines. Others provide fixed-term loans with predictable schedules. Custody models range from federally chartered banks to self-custody multisig setups. This guide compares the best options for borrowing against your Bitcoin and Ethereum, so you can choose the platform that fits your needs

How Borrowing Against BTC and ETH Actually Works

A crypto-backed loan uses your digital assets as collateral. You deposit BTC or ETH with a lender, and they provide cash or stablecoins in return . The amount you can borrow depends on your Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio. Most platforms offer between 50% and 60% LTV for Bitcoin and Ethereum . If you pledge $100,000 in BTC, you might borrow $50,000 to $60,000.

The core advantage is tax efficiency. Borrowing against your crypto does not trigger a taxable event in most jurisdictions . You avoid the capital gains tax that would come with selling. You also keep upside exposure—if Bitcoin or Ethereum rises during your loan term, those gains remain yours .

The risk is price volatility. If your collateral drops, your LTV rises automatically. If it crosses the platform's liquidation threshold, they may sell some of your collateral .

Comparing Top Platforms: Rates, LTV, and Collateral Options

Different platforms offer different structures for borrowing against BTC and ETH. Here is how the leading options compare:

Nexo offers a revolving credit line with no fixed repayment schedule . You can draw, repay, and borrow again without reapplying. Rates start at 1.9% APR for Platinum-tier clients at 20% LTV. Nexo accepts over 100 assets, including BTC and ETH at 50% LTV . There is no origination fee.

Arch Lending provides fixed-term loans with rates starting at 7.25% APR and 60% LTV . Collateral is held with Anchorage Digital, a federally chartered crypto bank, and backed by a $250 million insurance policy. Arch has a strict no-rehypothecation policy—your collateral is never lent out .

Ledn offers fixed 12-month loans at 10.4% APR plus a 2% origination fee—effectively around 12.4% . Ledn accepts BTC and ETH with custody through BitGo. It has processed over $6.5 billion in loans since 2018 .

Salt Lending provides fixed-term loans from 12 to 60 months. Rates range from 9.95% to 14.45% APR based on LTV. Salt accepts BTC, ETH, USDC, and USDT .

Figure offers crypto-backed loans with rates from 8.91% to 11.50% depending on LTV . Figure uses decentralized self-custody with MPC technology and does not rehypothecate collateral .

Revolving Credit Line vs. Fixed-Term Loan

The most important structural choice is between a revolving credit line and a fixed-term loan.

A revolving credit line—offered by Nexo—has no fixed end date and no minimum repayment. You borrow only what you need and pay interest only on the amount you actually use . The line stays open after repayment, so you can draw again without a new application. This structure works well if you want ongoing access to liquidity.

A fixed-term loan—offered by Ledn, Arch, and Salt—gives you a lump sum with a set repayment schedule . This structure provides predictability: you know exactly when the loan ends and what you owe. It works well for borrowers who want a clear timeline.

Neither is universally better. The right choice depends on whether you value flexibility or predictability.

Common Questions About Bitcoin and Ethereum Collateral Loans

Can I use both Bitcoin and Ethereum as collateral on the same platform?

Yes. Platforms like Nexo, Arch Lending, and Figure accept both BTC and ETH as collateral . Some platforms allow you to combine multiple assets to back a single credit line .

What is the typical LTV for Bitcoin and Ethereum loans?

Most platforms cap LTV at 50% for BTC and ETH . Stablecoins often qualify for higher LTVs (up to 90%). Some platforms like Arch Lending offer up to 60% LTV on BTC and ETH .

Is my collateral safe if the platform fails?

Conclusion

Borrowing against your Bitcoin and Ethereum lets you access liquidity without selling. The three key takeaways are: 1) Most platforms offer 50–60% LTV on BTC and ETH, with rates ranging from under 2% to over 14%. 2) Choose between a revolving credit line (flexibility) and a fixed-term loan (predictability). 3) Custody matters—regulated platforms with insurance and no rehypothecation offer stronger protection.
